name: callsmith.menu
description: The intake question tree. Each group is one MCQ step. Options carry a `maps` block the resolver reads to resolve providers and flags. A group with a `when` predicate only runs when the predicate holds against earlier answers. This file is the single source of truth for `callsmith spec`.

groups.title: Where does the conversation happen?
groups.help: Pick the channel the caller uses to reach the agent. This decides whether telephony is in the stack at all.

options.label: Inbound phone call (PSTN)
options.blurb: Customers call a number; the agent answers.

options.label: Outbound phone call (PSTN)
options.blurb: The agent dials out to a lead/customer.

options.label: Web voice chat (browser)
options.blurb: In-browser mic/speaker over WebRTC or WebSocket.

options.label: App-to-app voice
options.blurb: Mobile/desktop app voice via a realtime room.

options.label: WhatsApp voice notes
options.blurb: Async voice messages transcribed and replied to.

groups.title: How should the agent generate speech?
groups.help: Realtime speech-to-speech is lowest latency but harder to control. Cascaded (STT -> LLM -> TTS) is easier to debug, cheaper, and lets you swap parts independently.

options.label: Realtime speech-to-speech
options.blurb: One model handles audio in and audio out. Lowest latency.

options.label: Cascaded STT -> LLM -> TTS
options.blurb: Separate transcription, reasoning, synthesis. Most flexible.

options.label: Hybrid (realtime + fallback)
options.blurb: Realtime with a cascaded fallback path.

groups.title: Which telephony provider carries the call?

options.label: Exotel
options.blurb: India/SEA telephony, media-stream WebSocket.

options.label: Twilio
options.blurb: Global telephony, Media Streams WebSocket.

options.label: Plivo
options.blurb: Telephony with XML + media streaming.

options.label: Telnyx
options.blurb: Telephony with Call Control + media.

options.label: Vonage
options.blurb: Global telephony, Voice API media streaming.

groups.title: How should the pipeline be orchestrated?
groups.help: The orchestration layer owns audio frames, turn-taking, and interruption. LiveKit normalizes audio server-side; Pipecat is a frame pipeline you host; a custom bridge gives full control but full responsibility.

options.label: LiveKit Agents
options.blurb: Realtime room + SIP trunk; audio normalized to 16k PCM.

options.label: Pipecat
options.blurb: Frame pipeline; transports decode telephony audio at the edge.

options.label: Custom FastAPI bridge
options.blurb: You write the WebSocket bridge and audio path.

groups.title: Who should own the realtime media infrastructure?
groups.help: This decides the operations tradeoff. Managed cloud gives more native media features and less maintenance. Self-hosted gives control but you own scaling, deploys, audio cleanup, and debugging.

options.label: Managed cloud
options.blurb: Provider/cloud owns media rooms, SIP/WebRTC edge, and most runtime features. Higher platform cost, lowest maintenance.

options.label: Cloud edge + self-hosted worker
options.blurb: Provider handles edge media; your worker owns business logic, traces, tools, and deploy reliability.

options.label: Self-hosted
options.blurb: You host the media worker/bridge. Lowest platform fee, but you own codec paths, noise/echo cleanup, scaling, and incident response.

groups.title: Which realtime speech-to-speech model?

options.label: Gemini Live
options.blurb: 16k PCM in, 24k PCM out. Strong multilingual.

options.label: OpenAI Realtime
options.blurb: 24k PCM in/out (or μ-law 8k). Tool-calling native.

groups.title: Which speech-to-text?

options.label: Deepgram (Nova-3)
options.blurb: Streaming 16k PCM. Fast, accurate.

options.label: AssemblyAI
options.blurb: Streaming + universal real-time.

groups.title: Which reasoning model?

options.label: GPT-5.5
options.blurb: OpenAI, tool-calling.

options.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6
options.blurb: Anthropic, strong reasoning.

options.label: Gemini 3.5 Flash
options.blurb: Google, good at Hinglish.

groups.title: Which text-to-speech?

options.label: ElevenLabs
options.blurb: Streaming MP3/PCM. Very natural.

options.label: Sarvam
options.blurb: Indian-language TTS, low latency.

options.label: Cartesia
options.blurb: Sub-200ms streaming.

groups.title: Which voice activity detection (VAD)?
groups.help: VAD detects when the user starts/stops speaking. It drives barge-in (interruption) and turn-taking. Silero is the standard in both Pipecat and LiveKit.

options.label: Silero VAD
options.blurb: Most accurate neural VAD. Standard in Pipecat and LiveKit.

options.label: Deepgram Endpointing
options.blurb: Built into Deepgram STT. Lower accuracy than Silero but no extra dependency.

options.label: WebRTC VAD
options.blurb: Lightweight GMM-based. Fastest but least accurate. No model download.

groups.title: Which language(s)?
Should callers be able to interrupt the agent?

options.label: Yes, required (full-duplex)
options.blurb: Caller speech cancels agent output.

groups.title: Which operational profile fits best?
groups.help: A preset of endpointing, interruption sensitivity, noise handling, silence timeout, call-duration cap, greeting, voice style, and language fallback. Pick the closest fit; every value is overridable later in the generated voice_ux.py.

options.label: Support (balanced)
options.blurb: Balanced endpointing, normal interruption, warm voice, 30-min cap. Default for support and booking.

options.label: Fast IVR (aggressive)
options.blurb: Quick turn closure, high interruption sensitivity, faster speech, 10-min cap. Short transactional calls.

options.label: Careful (slow)
options.blurb: Conservative endpointing, low interruption, slower speech, 60-min cap, ask caller for language. Hesitant callers.

groups.title: How much audio cleanup should the agent use?
groups.help: This covers noise suppression, echo cancellation, and automatic gain control. The resolver records who owns each feature for the selected hosting/orchestration stack.

options.label: Provider/framework default
options.blurb: Use native WebRTC/SIP/framework cleanup when available. Good default for production.

options.label: Voice focus
options.blurb: More aggressive speech isolation for noisy callers. Watch for clipped soft speech.

options.label: Raw / lowest latency
options.blurb: Disable cleanup for controlled devices or lab testing. Lowest latency, least forgiving.

options.label: Self-hosted DSP
options.blurb: Your app owns cleanup modules. Required when custom hosting needs explicit DSP controls.

groups.title: How deep should production debugging be?
groups.help: Voice bugs are timing bugs. Pick how much trace detail and temporary audio evidence the generated project should keep.

options.label: Production timeline
options.blurb: Per-call event timeline, latency, interruption, tool, reconnect, and cost metrics. No raw audio retained.

options.label: Forensic
options.blurb: Frame-level trace plus short redacted audio capture window for hard barge-in/noise/echo bugs.

options.label: Lean metrics only
options.blurb: Aggregate metrics with lower trace sampling. Cheapest and quietest, but harder to debug incidents.
